bands.1:
You have won Narra the Teller's badge. Now he is on your side.

"The tide goes out at midnight," says Narra. "It comes back in 45 minutes. Then the cave is the sea's story."

"Story," squeaks Echobat, his tiny bat. "Story."

Indi's disguises are big headphones made of coconuts. Mo's coconut still has milk in it. It drips down his neck.

Gus holds up a bottle. "The Burp Bottle! Three weeks of my best burps. That's not gross. That's science."

At midnight, you splash along the sandbar to the cave. Two Goldies guard the gold door. They wear big headphones.

Gus opens the bottle next to their microphones. BRRRAAAP! The Goldies stumble away, dizzy.

Zed types MAXXSOUNDSAMAZING. The door opens.

Inside is the Echo Studio. It is padded with gold foam. Cages line the wall. There are Duettle twins, Dashling hatchlings and a Murkle.

On the desk are tapes. Each one says, "HAPPY NOISES (ME)."

Zed plays one. First you hear hatchlings crying. Then you hear Maxx in a squeaky voice. "Squee! Thank you, Maxx! You're my hero!"

"Nailed it," says the real Maxx. "That's Maxx-imum content."

"That is not the hatchlings' story," says Narra. "That is his."

You put the tapes in your bag. That is the proof.

Wren opens the cages. Then water rushes over the floor. The tide is coming back! The Goldies are coming back too.

Echobat flies out. It shouts in Maxx's voice, "Goldies! Back to the yacht!"

The Goldies run off.

You splash back with hatchlings in every pocket. On the beach, the Dashlings race into the sea.

On the boat, Zed plays one last tape. It is a deep, sad song from far out at sea. The label says, "THE BIG ONE. Play this to bring her close. Bring the biggest net."

Narra goes pale. "Only Old Glimmer sings like that," he whispers. "Nobody has heard her in fifty years."
bands.2:

"The tide goes out at midnight," he says, "and comes back at quarter to one. That is the crew's story, Captain. Forty-five minutes. After that, it is the sea's story."

"Story," squeaks Echobat from his hat. "Story."

"That's a fifty-fifty chance of a flooded cave," says Tully. "Still better odds than the Reef Rays."

Indi's disguises are sound engineers, with giant headphones made from coconut halves. Mo's coconut still has milk in it, and it dribbles down his neck whenever he nods.

Gus holds up a corked bottle. "The Burp Bottle," he whispers. "Three weeks of my finest burps. That's not gross. That's science."

At midnight, the sandbar rises out of the lagoon like a road. You splash along it to the cave. Two Goldies sit by the gold door, wearing enormous headphones.

Gus uncorks the bottle right beside their microphones. BRRRAAAAAP! The Goldies rip off their headphones and stagger out onto the sand, too dizzy to stand.

Zed types MAXXSOUNDSAMAZING, and the door clicks open. "Speedrun," he grins.

The Echo Studio is padded with gold foam. There's a desk covered in sliders and a glass booth with a gold microphone. Cages line the back wall: Duettle twins, Dashling hatchlings and a sulky Murkle hiding in its own ink.

On the desk is a stack of tapes. Every label says, "HAPPY NOISES (ME)."

Zed plays one. First comes the real sound: hatchlings squealing in fright. Then, on top, comes Maxx in a squeaky voice. "Squee! Squee! Thank you, Maxx! You're my hero!"

Then, in his normal voice: "Nailed it. That's Maxx-imum content."

"That is not the hatchlings' story," Narra says softly. "That is his."

"His," says Echobat. "His."

You pack the tapes into your waterproof bag. That's the proof.

Wren opens the cages. Then water swirls across the floor. The tide is coming back early, and so are the Goldies.

Echobat has heard Maxx so often that it can copy his voice perfectly. It flies out over the Goldies and shouts, "Goldies! Back to the yacht, now!"

The Goldies salute and run.

You splash back along the sinking sandbar, with hatchlings in every pocket. On the beach, the Dashlings race for the sea, and this time nothing stops them.

Back on the boat, Zed plays the last tape. It's a deep, slow, beautiful song, recorded far out at sea. The label says, "THE BIG ONE. Play this to lure her close. Bring the biggest net."

Narra goes pale. "Only Old Glimmer sings like that," he whispers. "And nobody has heard her for fifty years."

"The tide goes out at midnight," he says, "and comes back at quarter to one. That is the crew's story, Captain: forty-five minutes to get in and get out. After that, it becomes the sea's story."

Along the back wall are tanks and cages: Duettle twins, Dashling hatchlings, a sulky Murkle hiding in its own cloud of ink, and a Sidlewink clicking nervously.

First comes the real sound, recorded on the beach: hatchlings squealing in fright. Then, on top of it, a second track begins. It's Maxx, alone in the booth, in a high, squeaky voice. "Squee! Squee! Thank you, Maxx! You're my hero, Maxx! Squeeeee!"

"His," says Echobat. "His."

You scoop the tapes into your waterproof bag. That's the evidence.

Wren and Narra open the cages. The Dashlings head straight for the door, because a Dashling only ever wants one thing: the sea. The Duettles argue about who should go first, and who rescued whom, until Wren picks them both up at once.

Then water swirls across the floor. The tide is coming back early. Outside, the Goldies have recovered and are splashing back along the sandbar. You're trapped.

Echobat has spent so many nights near this cave that it can copy Maxx's voice perfectly. It flutters out of the cave mouth, high over the Goldies' heads, and shouts, "Goldies! Back to the yacht, now! Smash that heart button!"

The Goldies salute and race off towards their boat.

You splash back along the sinking sandbar, waist-deep, with hatchlings tucked into every pocket. Behind you, the cave mouth slips under the waves. On the beach, the Dashlings sprint for the water, and this time nothing stops them.

Back on the boat, Zed plays the last tape in the pile, just to check. It isn't happy noises. It's the deep, slow, beautiful song of something enormous, recorded far out at sea. On the label, in gold pen, Maxx has written: "THE BIG ONE. Play this to lure her close. Bring the biggest net."

Narra the Teller goes pale beneath his straw hat. "Narra knows only one Creature with a song like that," he whispers. "Old Glimmer, the great glowing ray. And nobody has heard her sing for fifty years."
